title: Derived additive coyoneda computes maps from a single complex
statement: Let A be a Grothendieck abelian category with hom universe u and compatible derived categories of A and additive groups [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every object P of A and integer n, the functor K maps to Hom(P[0],K[n]) on D(A) is naturally isomorphic, as an additive-group-valued functor, to degree-n homology of the unbounded right derived functor of additive Hom(P,-).

source.place: Declaration docstring: evaluation on K-injective resolutions and locally finite free tensor calculation; Stacks 08JJ and HRS Lemma 5.3(2)

proof.text: For a K-injective complex J, the degree-zero cycles of Hom(P,J) are chain maps from P[0], and the boundaries are null-homotopic maps. Thus zeroth homology is the additive group of homotopy classes. Localization at quasi-isomorphisms is fully faithful into a K-injective target. Compose these two additive equivalences. Their naturality follows by postcomposition on representatives; this is implemented by the proved abstract_singleHomologyEquiv and abstract_kInjectiveQuotientEquiv infrastructure of LocallyFreeDerivedHom, without using its ringed-site theorem.

source.place: Declaration docstring: evaluation on K-injective resolutions and locally finite free tensor calculation; Stacks 08JJ and HRS Lemma 5.3(2)

proof.text: Take the functorial K-injective resolution I with quasi-isomorphism eta. The derived comparison for additive Hom(P,-) is invertible on I(K). Combine its inverse with the preceding additive equivalence; naturality makes these componentwise isomorphisms a natural isomorphism after I. Applying localization to eta gives natural isomorphisms before and after I, so conjugation removes I. Descend this natural isomorphism through the localization Q to D(A).

proof.text: Whisker the degree-zero isomorphism by shift n. Commute the total right derived functor with shift, then use the cohomology-shift isomorphism H0(K[n]) = Hn(K). This produces the displayed isomorphism for every integer n.

lean.statement:
theorem derived_coyoneda_evaluation (P : A) (n : ℤ) : Nonempty
    (shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory A) n ⋙
        preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (op ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0).obj P)) ≅
      (preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (op P)).rightDerivedFunctor ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n)
